summary: Partial continuation preserving the 106-node sieve and Maynard checkpoint. Adds explicit logarithmic/product sieve dimensions, strict absolute remainder mass, a quantitative family level, finite weighted Rankin/Euler estimates and their dimension-controlled applications, a conditional mass-and-cutoff Eratosthenes bound, the corrected Brun combinatorial sieve and an endpoint-safe roughness-to-almost-prime transfer. All six stages have a reconciled target inventory including the added paper routes, but the full target-level pass is unfinished; no stage is closed and every node is unchecked.

nodes.title: Weighted divisibility interchange
nodes.statement: For every coefficient function c:N→R, sum_{d|P} c(d) A_d = sum_{n in A} w(n) sum_{d|gcd(P,n)} c(d).
hypotheses: s is the existing BoundingSieve: P=s.prodPrimes, A=s.support, w=s.weights, X=s.totalMass, nu=s.nu; A_d=s.multSum(d), R_d=s.rem(d), S=s.siftedSum. Divisors are positive natural divisors.
c is arbitrary; its values need not be nonnegative.
proofSteps: Expand each A_d and interchange two finite sums; retain c(d) with its sign.
For each n, divisibility by both P and n is equivalent to divisibility by gcd(P,n). Since P is nonzero and gcd(P,n) divides P, apply Nat.divisors_filter_dvd_of_dvd to identify the inner finite set.
acceptance: For P=1 this reduces to c(1) times the total support weight, including a possible weight at zero.
For P=6 the four divisor coefficients account separately for 1,2,3,6; no coprimality condition is imposed on n.

nodes.title: Legendre error for arbitrary local residue conditions
nodes.statement: Under the proper local-set hypotheses, let S=Σ_{a∈A,∀p∈Q,x(a) mod p∉Ωp}w(a), ρ(p)=card(Ωp)/p and P=∏_{p∈Q,Ωp nonempty}p. Then |S−X∏_{p∈Q}(1−ρ(p))| ≤ Σ_{d|P}|Σ_{a∈A,∀p∈primeFactors(d),x(a) mod p∈Ωp}w(a)−X∏_{p∈primeFactors(d)}ρ(p)|.
hypotheses: A is a finite index set, x maps indices to integers, w is real-valued and nonnegative on A, Q is a finite set consisting of primes, Ωp is a finite subset of ZMod p for each natural p, card(Ωp)
The divisor sum includes d=1; X need not equal the indexed total weight. No analytic remainder, dimension or distribution hypothesis is implied.
proofSteps: Apply the inherited legendre-error theorem to the residue-class constructor.
Use residue-class-siftedsum to replace its sifted sum by S, and residue-euler-product to restore the full Q Euler product.
Expand the existing signed remainder using residue-class-multsum. Every d|P is positive, so the existing prodPrimeFactors evaluation gives the displayed product of local densities.
Reorder real multiplication to place X first. All errors remain inside absolute values; no source-claimed cutoff or quantitative estimate is imported.
acceptance: All-empty local data give the identity |Σw−X|≤|Σw−X|, retaining the mass-normalization error at d=1.
The indexed Goldbach polynomial example retains seven parameters, not four image points.
Even labels larger than the original sample bound are allowed; quantitative sieve applications still need independently proved cutoff or tail hypotheses.

sources.match: Worker-derived realization of the source's arbitrary local conditions in the existing Mathlib divisibility carrier. Finite weighted fibers, prime-support algebra and the multiplicative extension are imported from the pinned library; no analytic remainder estimate is attributed to this adapter.

nodes.title: Vanishing Gram row detects the zero vector
nodes.statement: For each i∈I, rᵢ=0 if and only if yᵢ=0.
hypotheses: 𝕜 is ℝ or ℂ, represented by the existing RCLike structure; E is a normed inner-product space over 𝕜. Completeness and finite dimensionality are not assumed.
I is a finite indexing type, possibly empty unless stated otherwise; y:I→E is an arbitrary indexed family. Repetitions, zero vectors and linear dependence are allowed.

Use Mathlib's inner product, conjugate-linear in the first argument. Write Gᵢⱼ=⟨yᵢ,yⱼ⟩ and rᵢ=Σⱼ|Gᵢⱼ|. This is the existing Matrix.gram and an ordinary finite real sum, not a new carrier. Real division by zero is zero.
proofSteps: Each summand defining rᵢ is nonnegative. The diagonal term |⟨yᵢ,yᵢ⟩| is at most rᵢ by finite-sum monotonicity.
If rᵢ=0 the diagonal inner product is zero, so the existing positive-definite inner-product lemma gives yᵢ=0. Conversely, a zero vector makes every entry of its row zero.
acceptance: A family containing a zero vector has a zero row without making any other denominator invalid.
A nonzero vector always has positive row sum, even in a dependent family.

sources.locator: p.402, Proposition 1, denominator in the statement
sources.match: Explicit boundary lemma for the source's row denominator. The diagonal argument fills the zero-vector convention without imposing the unnecessary hypothesis that every vector is nonzero.

nodes.title: Gram-row bound for a finite linear combination
nodes.statement: For every scalar family c:I→𝕜, ‖Σᵢcᵢyᵢ‖² ≤ Σᵢ|cᵢ|²rᵢ.
hypotheses: 𝕜 is ℝ or ℂ, represented by the existing RCLike structure; E is a normed inner-product space over 𝕜. Completeness and finite dimensionality are not assumed.
I is a finite indexing type, possibly empty unless stated otherwise; y:I→E is an arbitrary indexed family. Repetitions, zero vectors and linear dependence are allowed.

Use Mathlib's inner product, conjugate-linear in the first argument. Write Gᵢⱼ=⟨yᵢ,yⱼ⟩ and rᵢ=Σⱼ|Gᵢⱼ|. This is the existing Matrix.gram and an ordinary finite real sum, not a new carrier. Real division by zero is zero.
proofSteps: Expand the squared norm as the real part of Σᵢⱼ conjugate(cᵢ)cⱼGᵢⱼ, using the existing Gram quadratic identity, or its finite inner-product sum laws.
Bound each real part by its modulus and then use 2|cᵢ||cⱼ|≤|cᵢ|²+|cⱼ|²; this follows by expanding the nonnegative square (|cᵢ|−|cⱼ|)².
Interchange indices in the terms containing |cⱼ|². Norm symmetry of the inner product makes the two half-sums equal, leaving exactly Σᵢ|cᵢ|²rᵢ.
acceptance: The empty family gives 0≤0.
Repeated unit vectors with all coefficients 1 attain equality; no orthogonality is assumed.
Changing Gᵢⱼ to its real part without taking absolute values is invalid: the family 1,−1 has cancelling signed rows.

sources.locator: p.402, equation (4) in the proof of Proposition 1
sources.match: Same finite quadratic estimate, translated from the source's linear-first convention to Mathlib's conjugate-linear-first convention. Replacing a complex ordered expression by its real part is explicit.

nodes.title: Selberg's normalized projection defect bound
nodes.statement: Set cᵢ=⟨yᵢ,x⟩/rᵢ, casting the real denominator to 𝕜. Then ‖x−Σᵢcᵢyᵢ‖² ≤ ‖x‖²−Σᵢ|⟨x,yᵢ⟩|²/rᵢ.
hypotheses: 𝕜 is ℝ or ℂ, represented by the existing RCLike structure; E is a normed inner-product space over 𝕜. Completeness and finite dimensionality are not assumed.
I is a finite indexing type, possibly empty unless stated otherwise; y:I→E is an arbitrary indexed family. Repetitions, zero vectors and linear dependence are allowed.

Use Mathlib's inner product, conjugate-linear in the first argument. Write Gᵢⱼ=⟨yᵢ,yⱼ⟩ and rᵢ=Σⱼ|Gᵢⱼ|. This is the existing Matrix.gram and an ordinary finite real sum, not a new carrier. Real division by zero is zero.
x is any vector of E.
proofSteps: Use the existing norm_sub_sq expansion with the finite linear combination. Apply gram-row-quadratic to its squared norm.
For each i, conjugate symmetry and z·conjugate(z)=|z|² give Re(cᵢ⟨x,yᵢ⟩)=|⟨x,yᵢ⟩|²/rᵢ.
Since rᵢ≥0, scalar norm/division gives |cᵢ|²rᵢ=|⟨x,yᵢ⟩|²/rᵢ. Split rᵢ=0 before field cancellation; both sides of this identity are zero in that case.
Sum the two identities and collect the −2 and +1 contributions. Use the corrected single row sum, not the printed global sum of squared Gram entries recorded in E9.
acceptance: For x=1 and y=i in ℂ the coefficient is −i, and its multiple of y is 1. The opposite convention gives −1 and does not prove the defect estimate.
For x=1,y=2 in ℝ the corrected coefficient is 1/2 and the defect is zero; the printed coefficient 1/8 gives defect 9/16.

sources.match: The finite Bessel-defect argument with the coefficient misprint corrected explicitly in E9. No completeness or infinite series is used.

nodes.title: Selberg's weighted inner-product inequality
nodes.statement: Σᵢ |⟨x,yᵢ⟩|²/rᵢ ≤ ‖x‖².
hypotheses: 𝕜 is ℝ or ℂ, represented by the existing RCLike structure; E is a normed inner-product space over 𝕜. Completeness and finite dimensionality are not assumed.
I is a finite indexing type, possibly empty unless stated otherwise; y:I→E is an arbitrary indexed family. Repetitions, zero vectors and linear dependence are allowed.

Use Mathlib's inner product, conjugate-linear in the first argument. Write Gᵢⱼ=⟨yᵢ,yⱼ⟩ and rᵢ=Σⱼ|Gᵢⱼ|. This is the existing Matrix.gram and an ordinary finite real sum, not a new carrier. Real division by zero is zero.
x is any vector of E; zero rows contribute zero.
proofSteps: The left-hand squared norm in selberg-defect is nonnegative. Move the weighted sum to the other side.
The proof is finite over either scalar field. Thus the Hilbert-space statement extends to normed inner-product spaces without a completeness assumption.
acceptance: An empty or all-zero family has weighted sum zero.
For a single nonzero vector this is Cauchy–Schwarz after dividing by its squared norm.
For x=1 and real y=(1,2), the two terms are 1/3 and 4/6, summing to 1; replacing the denominators by their squares fails already at y=1/2.
For an orthonormal family all rows equal one, so the result agrees with the existing finite Bessel inequality; it does not rebuild the orthonormal theory.

sources.match: The source's stronger weighted theorem, with a precise zero-division convention and derived removal of the unused completeness hypothesis.

nodes.title: Inner-product bound from a uniform Gram row estimate
nodes.statement: If B≥0 and rᵢ≤B for every i, then Σᵢ|⟨x,yᵢ⟩|² ≤ ‖x‖²B.
hypotheses: 𝕜 is ℝ or ℂ, represented by the existing RCLike structure; E is a normed inner-product space over 𝕜. Completeness and finite dimensionality are not assumed.
I is a finite indexing type, possibly empty unless stated otherwise; y:I→E is an arbitrary indexed family. Repetitions, zero vectors and linear dependence are allowed.

Use Mathlib's inner product, conjugate-linear in the first argument. Write Gᵢⱼ=⟨yᵢ,yⱼ⟩ and rᵢ=Σⱼ|Gᵢⱼ|. This is the existing Matrix.gram and an ordinary finite real sum, not a new carrier. Real division by zero is zero.
x∈E; B is a real nonnegative bound, not a new bound predicate.
proofSteps: If rᵢ=0 then gram-row-zero makes yᵢ=0, hence its unweighted numerator is zero.
For rᵢ>0, multiply rᵢ≤B by the nonnegative quotient |⟨x,yᵢ⟩|²/rᵢ. This bounds the unweighted numerator by B times that quotient.
Sum and multiply selberg-weighted-inner by B≥0. This form needs no maximum and therefore supports the empty family.
acceptance: B=0 forces every indexed vector zero.
For an empty family and x=1, allowing B=−1 would assert 0≤−1; the sign hypothesis is necessary in the empty case.

sources.locator: p.402, Proposition 1; p.403, reduction to uniform row bound (5)
sources.match: The direct finite consequence used in the paper's large-sieve proof; the analytic construction and proof of (5) are separate remaining work.

nodes.title: Bombieri–Selberg Gram-row inequality
nodes.statement: For nonempty I, Σᵢ|⟨x,yᵢ⟩|² ≤ ‖x‖² maxᵢ∈I rᵢ.
hypotheses: 𝕜 is ℝ or ℂ, represented by the existing RCLike structure; E is a normed inner-product space over 𝕜. Completeness and finite dimensionality are not assumed.
I is a finite indexing type, possibly empty unless stated otherwise; y:I→E is an arbitrary indexed family. Repetitions, zero vectors and linear dependence are allowed.

Use Mathlib's inner product, conjugate-linear in the first argument. Write Gᵢⱼ=⟨yᵢ,yⱼ⟩ and rᵢ=Σⱼ|Gᵢⱼ|. This is the existing Matrix.gram and an ordinary finite real sum, not a new carrier. Real division by zero is zero.
x∈E and I is nonempty; use the existing finite supremum, not a chosen default maximum.
proofSteps: Take B to be the existing finite supremum of the real row sums. Every row is bounded by it.
Choose an index only to infer B≥0 from the nonnegative row at that index; no maximizing vector or Gram inverse is needed.
Apply bombieri-row-bound. Empty families are covered by that lemma instead of assigning an artificial real maximum.
acceptance: For m repeated copies of a unit vector and x that vector, both sides equal m, including the Gram off-diagonal contributions.
For y=(1,2) and x=1 over ℝ the unweighted sum is 5 and the maximum row is 6.
Taking the maximum of individual entries instead of row sums fails on repeated unit vectors.

sources.match: Exactly routed item PAPER-BENNETT-SIKSEK-20/45, with nonempty indexing explicit and the proof supplied by Bombieri 1971 Proposition 1.
Derived unweighted maximum form of the original stronger theorem.

nodes.title: Diagonal and off-diagonal Gram estimate
nodes.statement: If D,C≥0, ‖yᵢ‖²≤D for every i, and |⟨yᵢ,yⱼ⟩|≤C whenever i≠j, then Σᵢ|⟨x,yᵢ⟩|² ≤ ‖x‖²(D+(|I|−1)₊C), where (|I|−1)₊ is natural truncated subtraction.
hypotheses: 𝕜 is ℝ or ℂ, represented by the existing RCLike structure; E is a normed inner-product space over 𝕜. Completeness and finite dimensionality are not assumed.
I is a finite indexing type, possibly empty unless stated otherwise; y:I→E is an arbitrary indexed family. Repetitions, zero vectors and linear dependence are allowed.

Use Mathlib's inner product, conjugate-linear in the first argument. Write Gᵢⱼ=⟨yᵢ,yⱼ⟩ and rᵢ=Σⱼ|Gᵢⱼ|. This is the existing Matrix.gram and an ordinary finite real sum, not a new carrier. Real division by zero is zero.
x∈E; I may be empty. D and C are real nonnegative constants.
proofSteps: For an index i, use the existing additive companion of mul_prod_erase to separate its diagonal term from the remaining finite row.
The diagonal norm is ‖yᵢ‖². Bound the remaining |I|−1 terms individually by C; the existing erase-cardinality identity counts them exactly.
Thus each row is bounded by D+(|I|−1)₊C, a nonnegative number. Apply bombieri-row-bound, whose empty-family case requires no index choice.

For nonempty I, division by |I| and (|I|−1)/|I|≤1 gives the normalized bound (Σᵢ|⟨x,yᵢ⟩|²)/|I|≤‖x‖²(D/|I|+C) used in Bennett–Siksek. This is routine real arithmetic, not an analytic estimate of D or C.
acceptance: The empty family satisfies 0≤‖x‖²D and the singleton case has no off-diagonal contribution.
For m≥1 repeated unit vectors, D=C=1 gives equality with constant m.
For an orthonormal family D=1,C=0 recovers the finite Bessel bound. No arithmetic character-correlation or prime-number theorem bound is assumed implicitly.

nodes.title: Multiplicity of an integer difference
nodes.statement: For M∈ℕ and n∈ℤ, the number of ordered pairs 0≤a,b<M with a−b=n is M−|n|, using natural truncated subtraction M−n.natAbs.
hypotheses: M may be zero; the difference a−b is in ℤ, not natural subtraction.
proofSteps: For n≥0, send b in 0,…,M−n−1 to (b+n,b). For n<0, send a in 0,…,M−|n|−1 to (a,a+|n|). These are inverse coordinate projections on the filtered pair set.
Check the empty ranges when |n|≥M and M=0 before using endpoint arithmetic. The native finite-cardinality bijection and interval count give the common truncated value.
acceptance: M=3,n=−1 gives two pairs; M=3,n=3 gives none. Natural subtraction inside the filter would incorrectly count extra pairs at n=0.

nodes.title: Triangular Fourier sum as a squared modulus
nodes.statement: For every M∈ℕ and t∈ℝ, Σ_{n=−M}^{M}T_M(n)e(nt)=K_M(t), with the real right side cast to ℂ.
hypotheses: Use only local expressions e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ), T_M(n)=max(0,M−|n|), W_{N,L}(n)=(T_{N+L}(n)−T_N(n))/L, and K_M(t)=|Σ_{k=0}^{M−1}e(kt)|². The latter is the unnormalized finite Fejér expression, not a new kernel carrier. Cast naturals/integers to the displayed scalar field.
proofSteps: Expand the squared modulus of Σ_{a<M}e(at) as its product with its complex conjugate. The native Fourier character laws turn each pair term into e((a−b)t).
Group the finite pair sum by its integer difference in [−M,M], using the additive companions of the cited finite product/fiber lemmas. Every pair's difference belongs to that interval.
Apply difference-pair-count to each fiber and cast its truncated natural value to max(0,M−|n|). The endpoints ±M have coefficient zero, also when M=0.
acceptance: At t=0 the sum is M², not M; no normalized Fejér kernel is being used.
For M=1 the expression is constantly 1; for M=0 it is zero.

sources.locator: p.403, displayed definition and evaluation of K_M
sources.match: Finite coefficient expansion that the paper suppresses; no convergence or infinite Fourier-series theorem is needed.

nodes.title: Sine quotient for a finite Fourier sum
nodes.statement: If sin(πt)≠0, then K_M(t)=(sin(πMt)/sin(πt))² for every M∈ℕ.
hypotheses: Use only local expressions e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ), T_M(n)=max(0,M−|n|), W_{N,L}(n)=(T_{N+L}(n)−T_N(n))/L, and K_M(t)=|Σ_{k=0}^{M−1}e(kt)|². The latter is the unnormalized finite Fejér expression, not a new kernel carrier. Cast naturals/integers to the displayed scalar field.
The nonzero denominator is essential. At integer t the finite sum is instead M, and K_M(t)=M²; a totalized quotient would incorrectly give zero.
proofSteps: Write e(kt)=e(t)^k using the native additive-character power law.
The native exponential-difference norm identity gives |e(t)−1|=2|sin(πt)|, so the hypothesis permits the native finite geometric-series formula.

Take norms of (e(t)^M−1)/(e(t)−1). Apply the same exponential identity to the numerator, square, cancel the factor 4, and commute scalar products to obtain the displayed real quotient. M=0 is valid without a separate nonempty-sum assumption.
acceptance: M=2,t=1/2 gives zero; M=1,t=1/2 gives one.
At t=0,M=3 the actual value is 9, demonstrating why the sine-denominator hypothesis cannot be omitted.

nodes.title: Piecewise taper weights and their bounds
nodes.statement: For L>0, W_{N,L}(n) equals 1 if |n|≤N, equals (N+L−|n|)/L if N<|n|≤N+L, and equals 0 otherwise. In all cases 0≤W_{N,L}(n)≤1.
hypotheses: Use only local expressions e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ), T_M(n)=max(0,M−|n|), W_{N,L}(n)=(T_{N+L}(n)−T_N(n))/L, and K_M(t)=|Σ_{k=0}^{M−1}e(kt)|². The latter is the unnormalized finite Fejér expression, not a new kernel carrier. Cast naturals/integers to the displayed scalar field.
N,L∈ℕ, n∈ℤ; all inequalities in this formula are real after casting.
proofSteps: Split at |n|≤N and |n|≤N+L. In each branch evaluate the two maxima defining T.
Since L>0, subtraction of the two affine expressions gives L on the core and a number between 0 and L on the taper. Divide by positive L. Outside both supports the numerator is zero.
acceptance: N=1,L=2,n=2 gives 1/2; at |n|=N the value is 1, and at |n|=N+L it is zero.
L=0 is excluded here; the totalized expression is zero everywhere, not an indicator of the core.

nodes.title: Finite tapered Fourier vector
nodes.statement: Construct φ_{N,L}(x) with coordinate k equal to √W_{N,L}(n_k)·e(−n_k x), as a vector in the existing finite Euclidean space. Real square roots are cast to ℂ.
hypotheses: Use only local expressions e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ), T_M(n)=max(0,M−|n|), W_{N,L}(n)=(T_{N+L}(n)−T_N(n))/L, and K_M(t)=|Σ_{k=0}^{M−1}e(kt)|². The latter is the unnormalized finite Fejér expression, not a new kernel carrier. Cast naturals/integers to the displayed scalar field.

nodes.title: Signed Gram kernel of tapered vectors
nodes.statement: For L>0, ⟨φ_{N,L}(x),φ_{N,L}(y)⟩=(K_{N+L}(x−y)−K_N(x−y))/L, with the real quotient cast to ℂ.
hypotheses: Use only local expressions e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ), T_M(n)=max(0,M−|n|), W_{N,L}(n)=(T_{N+L}(n)−T_N(n))/L, and K_M(t)=|Σ_{k=0}^{M−1}e(kt)|². The latter is the unnormalized finite Fejér expression, not a new kernel carrier. Cast naturals/integers to the displayed scalar field.

proofSteps: Expand the native finite inner product. The nonnegative square root has squared value W, and conjugation changes e(−n_kx) to e(n_kx), so the term is W(n_k)e(n_k(x−y)).
Reindex k to the integer interval [−(N+L),N+L] by n_k=k−(N+L), with inverse n↦n+N+L. Split the two triangular sums and divide by L.

The result is a signed real difference. Only after taking its absolute value does it give the norm of the inner product; E10 records the source display's missing absolute value on this difference.

nodes.title: Squared norm of the tapered Fourier vector
nodes.statement: For L>0, ‖φ_{N,L}(x)‖²=2N+L.
hypotheses: Use only local expressions e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ), T_M(n)=max(0,M−|n|), W_{N,L}(n)=(T_{N+L}(n)−T_N(n))/L, and K_M(t)=|Σ_{k=0}^{M−1}e(kt)|². The latter is the unnormalized finite Fejér expression, not a new kernel carrier. Cast naturals/integers to the displayed scalar field.
For natural N,L use the existing EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin (2(N+L)+1)), with frequency n_k=k−(N+L). Mathlib's inner product is conjugate-linear in its first argument. Every sum here is finite.
proofSteps: Set y=x in the signed Gram identity. Every phase in K_M(0) is one, so K_M(0)=M².
Use the native inner-self identity and expand ((N+L)²−N²)/L=2N+L, cancelling only after L>0.
acceptance: N=0,L=1 has squared norm 1; N=1,L=2 has squared norm 4.
This mass is not the ambient dimension 2(N+L)+1, and not merely the core length 2N+1.

nodes.title: Off-diagonal tapered Gram bound
nodes.statement: If L>0 and sin(π(x−y))≠0, then |⟨φ_{N,L}(x),φ_{N,L}(y)⟩|≤1/(L sin²(π(x−y))).
hypotheses: Use only local expressions e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ), T_M(n)=max(0,M−|n|), W_{N,L}(n)=(T_{N+L}(n)−T_N(n))/L, and K_M(t)=|Σ_{k=0}^{M−1}e(kt)|². The latter is the unnormalized finite Fejér expression, not a new kernel carrier. Cast naturals/integers to the displayed scalar field.

proofSteps: Put A=1/sin²(π(x−y)), which is positive. The sine-square formula and the native upper bound sin²≤1 give 0≤K_M(x−y)≤A for both M=N and M=N+L.
Two numbers in [0,A] have difference with absolute value at most A, not merely 2A. Apply this elementary interval bound to the corrected signed Gram formula and divide by positive L.
Do not assume the kernel difference nonnegative; its sign changes in the half-turn example.
acceptance: N=L=1,x−y=1/2 attains the bound 1, despite negative Gram value.
Coincident phases modulo one are excluded by the nonzero-sine hypothesis; totalized division cannot justify a zero upper bound there.

nodes.title: Large-sieve bound from cosecant row control
nodes.statement: Let x_i be a finite real family and C≥0. Suppose sin(π(x_i−x_j))≠0 for i≠j and Σ_{j≠i}1/sin²(π(x_i−x_j))≤C for every i. For L>0 and core-supported f, Σ_i|Σ_k f_k e(n_kx_i)|²≤‖f‖²(2N+L+C/L).
hypotheses: Use only local expressions e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ), T_M(n)=max(0,M−|n|), W_{N,L}(n)=(T_{N+L}(n)−T_N(n))/L, and K_M(t)=|Σ_{k=0}^{M−1}e(kt)|². The latter is the unnormalized finite Fejér expression, not a new kernel carrier. Cast naturals/integers to the displayed scalar field.
For natural N,L use the existing EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin (2(N+L)+1)), with frequency n_k=k−(N+L). Mathlib's inner product is conjugate-linear in its first argument. Every sum here is finite.
The indexing type may be empty. N,L∈ℕ, L>0, and f_k=0 whenever |n_k|>N. The explicit cosecant row bound is a hypothesis, not an inferred consequence of separation.
proofSteps: For each i split the Gram row into its diagonal and its erased off-diagonal sum using the native additive erase identity.
Use tapered-diagonal on the diagonal and tapered-offdiagonal term by term elsewhere. Factor 1/L out of the finite sum and use the assumed row bound C.
The resulting bound B=2N+L+C/L is nonnegative even for an empty family. Apply bombieri-row-bound to the family of tapered vectors and f.
Use norm symmetry of the inner product and tapered-fourier-pairing to identify every summand. No maximum or nonempty-family hypothesis is needed.

Do not replace the row hypothesis by the paper's final separation constant here: corrected bin packing, the cosecant sum, the integer taper choice, and interval translation/parity remain separate recorded work.
acceptance: The empty family gives 0≤‖f‖²B; a singleton has C=0.
This conditional theorem is not the full additive large-sieve theorem with constant length+2/δ.

nodes.title: Sine lower bound from circular distance
nodes.statement: For every real t, 4d(t)²≤sin²(πt).
hypotheses: Write d(t)=‖(t:UnitAddCircle)‖ using the native real circle of period one, and e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit). These are notation, not new carriers.
Finite point families x:ι→ℝ are δ-separated when δ≤d(x_i−x_j) for all distinct labels i,j. δ>0 is explicit; no assumption that the family is nonempty.
proofSteps: Put r=t−round t and a=|r|=d(t). Native rounding gives 0≤a≤1/2.
Integer π-shift invariance after squaring and the oddness of sine give sin²(πt)=sin²(πa). The sign of r and integer-shift sign disappear only after squaring.
Apply Real.le_sin_mul to y=2a: 2a≤sin(πa). Both sides are nonnegative, so square.
acceptance: At t=0 both sides vanish; at t=1/2 both sides equal one.
Positive d(t) implies sin(πt)≠0; the inequality does not falsely exclude integer t.

nodes.title: Two-point bound for circular radial bins
nodes.statement: For a δ-separated finite real family, fixed i and m∈ℕ, #{j≠i: floor(d(x_i−x_j)/δ)=m}≤2. No upper restriction on m is imposed.
hypotheses: Write d(t)=‖(t:UnitAddCircle)‖ using the native real circle of period one, and e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit). These are notation, not new carriers.
Finite point families x:ι→ℝ are δ-separated when δ≤d(x_i−x_j) for all distinct labels i,j. δ>0 is explicit; no assumption that the family is nonempty.
proofSteps: For each j reduce x_j−x_i to r_j=(x_j−x_i)−round(x_j−x_i)∈[−1/2,1/2). Its absolute value is d(x_i−x_j), by native norm symmetry.
Within one floor bin, each |r_j| lies in [mδ,(m+1)δ). Two representatives of the same sign therefore differ in absolute value by strictly less than δ. Zero cannot occur because j≠i and δ>0.
For j≠k, round_le applied to x_j−x_k and the integer round(x_j−x_i)−round(x_k−x_i) bounds d(x_j−x_k) by |r_j−r_k|. This contradicts separation for two distinct labels with the same sign.
Thus the map recording whether r_j<0 is injective from the bin into the two signs. Apply the native finite-cardinality inequality.
The representative of an antipode is −1/2, never +1/2. The unrestricted floor-bin statement keeps the final partial bin and exact distance 1/2; it corrects the proof coverage gap E11.
acceptance: With δ=3/10 and x=(0,2/5), the off-diagonal point lies in m=1 although (m+1)δ>1/2.
For δ=1/4 an antipode lies in m=2 and is counted once; bin zero is empty for j≠i.

nodes.title: Separated cosecant-square row bound
nodes.statement: For every row i of a δ-separated finite family with δ>0, Σ_{j≠i}1/sin²(π(x_i−x_j))≤π²/(12δ²).
hypotheses: Write d(t)=‖(t:UnitAddCircle)‖ using the native real circle of period one, and e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit). These are notation, not new carriers.
Finite point families x:ι→ℝ are δ-separated when δ≤d(x_i−x_j) for all distinct labels i,j. δ>0 is explicit; no assumption that the family is nonempty.
proofSteps: For j≠i separation gives positive distance, hence nonzero sine by circular-sine-square. Put m_j=floor(d(x_i−x_j)/δ); then m_j≥1 and d(x_i−x_j)≥m_jδ.
The sine bound implies 1/sin²(π(x_i−x_j))≤1/(4m_j²δ²). Group the erased finite sum by the finite image of m_j using native sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to.
Each fiber contains at most two labels by circular-bin-packing. The row is at most (1/(2δ²)) times the sum of 1/m² over that finite image.

Native hasSum_zeta_two and the additive form of prod_le_hasProd bound that nonnegative finite sum by π²/6. The zero natural term is zero but never occurs in the finite image. Multiplication yields π²/(12δ²).
acceptance: Empty off-diagonal sums and singleton point families are allowed.
This proves the row estimate without assuming δ≤1/2; if there is an off-diagonal point, that upper bound follows automatically.

nodes.title: Explicit positive integer taper width
nodes.statement: If 0<δ≤1/2 and L=floor(1/δ)∈ℕ, then L>0 and L+[π²/(12δ²)]/L≤2/δ.
hypotheses: Write d(t)=‖(t:UnitAddCircle)‖ using the native real circle of period one, and e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit). These are notation, not new carriers.
Finite point families x:ι→ℝ are δ-separated when δ≤d(x_i−x_j) for all distinct labels i,j. δ>0 is explicit; no assumption that the family is nonempty.
proofSteps: The floor inequalities give L≥2, Lδ≤1 and (L+1)δ>1. Set r=Lδ. Since L≥2, r>L/(L+1)≥2/3.
The native bound π<3.15 implies π²/12≤8/9. For 2/3≤r≤1, (r−2/3)(r−4/3)≤0, so r²−2r+8/9≤0.
Consequently r²+π²/12≤2r. Divide by positive rδ to obtain the stated taper bound.
This is a worker-derived explicit floor choice proving the source's desired bound, not a transcription of the source's nearest-integer choice to π/(√12δ). No claim is made that the choices coincide.
acceptance: For δ=2 the floor is zero: the hypothesis δ≤1/2 cannot be dropped from this taper-width lemma.

nodes.title: Large sieve on the centered finite core
nodes.statement: Let 0<δ≤1/2, L=floor(1/δ), N∈ℕ, and x be δ-separated. In EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin(2(N+L)+1)), write n_k=k−(N+L). If f_k=0 for |n_k|>N, then Σ_i|Σ_k f_k e(n_kx_i)|²≤‖f‖²(2N+2/δ).
hypotheses: Write d(t)=‖(t:UnitAddCircle)‖ using the native real circle of period one, and e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit). These are notation, not new carriers.
Finite point families x:ι→ℝ are δ-separated when δ≤d(x_i−x_j) for all distinct labels i,j. δ>0 is explicit; no assumption that the family is nonempty.
The ambient width is this chosen L; the theorem does not silently alter an arbitrary input vector's dimension.
proofSteps: Set C=π²/(12δ²)≥0. Separation and circular-sine-square supply every nonzero sine required by tapered-row-large-sieve.
Cosecant-row-bound supplies its row hypotheses. Integer-taper-choice supplies L>0 and L+C/L≤2/δ.
Apply the inherited conditional theorem to the same f, then multiply the scalar inequality by the nonnegative squared norm.
acceptance: N=0 is allowed; the single central coefficient is embedded in the stated larger native space.
The number 2N is a centered half-width parameter, not yet an arbitrary original interval length.

nodes.title: Centered interval coefficient vector
nodes.statement: For H,L∈ℕ and a:Fin H→ℂ, put N=floor(H/2), o=L+1−(H mod 2), and D=2(N+L)+1. Define intervalVector H L a∈EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin D) by coordinate k equal to Σ_{j∈Fin H} [k=o+j]a_j. The bracket is the ordinary finite indicator, not a new scalar or carrier.
hypotheses: Write d(t)=‖(t:UnitAddCircle)‖ using the native real circle of period one, and e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit). These are notation, not new carriers.
Finite point families x:ι→ℝ are δ-separated when δ≤d(x_i−x_j) for all distinct labels i,j. δ>0 is explicit; no assumption that the family is nonempty.
Natural subtraction in o is nontruncating because H mod 2≤1≤L+1; no positivity of H or L is required.
proofSteps: Use the native EuclideanSpace constructor on the finite coordinate function; no new coefficient-vector space or quotient is introduced.
The expression k=o+j uses natural indices. This fixes which endpoint is padded when H is even; the four promoted interfaces establish the usable support, norm and phase properties.
acceptance: Its uses and four discriminating tests are specified below.

nodes.title: Core support of the interval vector
nodes.statement: For H,L∈ℕ, N=floor(H/2) and n_k=k−(N+L), |n_k|>N implies (intervalVector H L a)_k=0.
hypotheses: Write d(t)=‖(t:UnitAddCircle)‖ using the native real circle of period one, and e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit). These are notation, not new carriers.
Finite point families x:ι→ℝ are δ-separated when δ≤d(x_i−x_j) for all distinct labels i,j. δ>0 is explicit; no assumption that the family is nonempty.
proofSteps: Write H=2N+ε with ε∈{0,1}. The offset is o=L+1−ε. For j<H, the occupied frequency is n_{o+j}=j+1−N−ε.
If ε=0, occupied frequencies are 1−N through N, so the −N endpoint is zero. If ε=1, they are −N through N. If H=0 there are no occupied coordinates.
Thus a coordinate outside [−N,N] cannot match o+j for any j; all indicator summands in interval-coordinate vanish.
acceptance: H=2 occupies frequencies 0 and 1, not −1 and 0 under this translation.
No separate cutoff assumption is passed to the final theorem.

nodes.title: Norm preservation under interval padding
nodes.statement: For every H,L∈ℕ and a:Fin H→ℂ, ‖intervalVector H L a‖²=Σ_j|a_j|².
hypotheses: Write d(t)=‖(t:UnitAddCircle)‖ using the native real circle of period one, and e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit). These are notation, not new carriers.

proofSteps: The index map j↦o+j is injective. Using H=2N+ε and o=L+1−ε, verify 0≤o+j<2(N+L)+1 for every j<H; H=0 is empty.
Apply EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq. At each occupied coordinate, the indicator sum is exactly its unique coefficient; unoccupied coordinates contribute zero.
Reindex the finite coordinate-square sum along the injective map, using singleton fibers of native sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to. No cross terms and no multiplicities occur.
acceptance: For complex (1,i) and H=2,L=1, the squared norm is 2.
The conclusion includes H=0 and L=0.

nodes.title: Fourier translation of the padded interval
nodes.statement: For M∈ℤ, H,L∈ℕ, a:Fin H→ℂ, x∈ℝ, N=floor(H/2), c=M+floor((H+1)/2), one has Σ_j a_j e((M+j+1)x)=e(cx)Σ_k(intervalVector H L a)_k e((k−(N+L))x).
hypotheses: Write d(t)=‖(t:UnitAddCircle)‖ using the native real circle of period one, and e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit). These are notation, not new carriers.
Finite point families x:ι→ℝ are δ-separated when δ≤d(x_i−x_j) for all distinct labels i,j. δ>0 is explicit; no assumption that the family is nonempty.
proofSteps: Expand interval-coordinate, interchange the finite sums and retain the unique coordinate k=o+j. The index is inside the ambient dimension by H=2N+ε.
The integer identity c+(o+j−(N+L))=M+j+1 holds for ε=0 and ε=1, since floor((H+1)/2)=N+ε.
The native additive character turns the frequency sum into a product. This is equivalently obtained from the existing subtraction/division law; multiply by the nonzero unit phase.
Keep the positive 2π Fourier phase and the original starting frequency M+1; do not replace c by M+N for odd H.

For H=1,M=0,a=(1),x=1/4 the original sum is i; this distinguishes the starting frequency M+1 from M and the positive phase from the negative phase.

nodes.title: Cardinality above the circle diameter
nodes.statement: If δ>1/2 and a finite real family is δ-separated modulo one, its indexing type has cardinality at most one.
hypotheses: Write d(t)=‖(t:UnitAddCircle)‖ using the native real circle of period one, and e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit). These are notation, not new carriers.
Finite point families x:ι→ℝ are δ-separated when δ≤d(x_i−x_j) for all distinct labels i,j. δ>0 is explicit; no assumption that the family is nonempty.
proofSteps: Two distinct labels would have δ≤d(x_i−x_j)≤1/2 by the native half-period bound, a contradiction.
Hence all labels are equal; the finite type is empty or a singleton.

nodes.title: Bombieri's additive large sieve
nodes.statement: Let M∈ℤ, H∈ℕ, a:Fin H→ℂ, δ>0 and x:ι→ℝ be a finite δ-separated family modulo one. Then Σ_i|Σ_{j=0}^{H−1}a_j e((M+j+1)x_i)|²≤(H+2/δ)Σ_{j=0}^{H−1}|a_j|².
hypotheses: Write d(t)=‖(t:UnitAddCircle)‖ using the native real circle of period one, and e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit). These are notation, not new carriers.
Finite point families x:ι→ℝ are δ-separated when δ≤d(x_i−x_j) for all distinct labels i,j. δ>0 is explicit; no assumption that the family is nonempty.
Empty coefficient and point families are allowed. No restriction δ≤1/2 or normalization of coefficients is imposed.
proofSteps: When 0<δ≤1/2, set N=floor(H/2), L=floor(1/δ), and f=intervalVector H L a. Its support is interval-support, so separated-core applies.
Use interval-phase and norm one of e(cx) to identify each original summand; interval-norm identifies the coefficient-square sum. Since 2floor(H/2)≤H, increase the nonnegative scalar bound to H+2/δ.

When δ>1/2, separation-card-small leaves at most one point. Native norm_sum_le gives |Σ_j a_j e(...)|≤Σ_j|a_j|. Squared finite Cauchy–Schwarz against the constant one gives its square at most HΣ_j|a_j|²; this is bounded by the claimed expression.
The empty point family gives zero on the left. H=0 also gives zero, so all branches include both degenerate cases.
acceptance: The theorem has the original interval length H, not the centered N.
It is Bombieri's H+2/δ constant, not the sharper H−1+1/δ large sieve and not a multiplicative-character or quadratic-symbol large sieve.

nodes.title: Circular separation of reduced fractions
nodes.statement: For natural a,b,p,q,Q with 0<p,q≤Q, a<p, b<q, gcd(a,p)=gcd(b,q)=1 and (a,p)≠(b,q), one has ‖(a/p−b/q:UnitAddCircle)‖≥1/Q².
hypotheses: Use e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit), the existing UnitAddCircle norm, and the native DirichletCharacter ℂ q, its conductor-based IsPrimitive predicate and its inverse. There is no new Fourier, character or Farey carrier.
proofSteps: Put t=a/p−b/q and z=round(t). Since both fractions lie in [0,1), t lies strictly between −1 and 1. If t were an integer, it would therefore be zero. Equality of the rational fractions would force a=b and p=q by the native reduced-fraction uniqueness theorem, contradicting the hypothesis.
The integer D=aq−bp−zpq is consequently nonzero. Thus |D|≥1. Clear only the positive denominators p and q to obtain |t−z|=|D|/(pq)≥1/(pq).

The native circle-norm formula identifies |t−z| with the required norm. Since pq≤Q² and Q>0, reciprocal monotonicity gives the result. This argument includes wraparound, not just the linear separation of real fractions.
acceptance: The sole reduced pair with numerator zero is (0,1); the endpoint 1/1 is excluded by a<p.
0/1 and 3/4 have circle distance 1/4 although their linear distance is 3/4.
Dropping coprimality allows labels (1,2) and (2,4) at the same point.

sources.match: Expands the integer-numerator spacing argument. Rat.div_int_inj supplies uniqueness; no Farey sequence definition, ordering or neighbour theorem is repeated.

nodes.title: Additive large sieve over reduced residues
nodes.statement: Σ_{1≤q≤Q}Σ_{u∈(Z/qZ)×}|S(val(u)/q)|² ≤ (H+2Q²)Σ_{j<H}|a_j|².
hypotheses: Use e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit), the existing UnitAddCircle norm, and the native DirichletCharacter ℂ q, its conductor-based IsPrimitive predicate and its inverse. There is no new Fourier, character or Farey carrier.
M is any integer, H and Q are natural numbers, and a:Fin H→ℂ is arbitrary. Write n_j=M+j+1 and S(t)=Σ_{j<H}a_j e(n_j t). Empty intervals and Q=0 are permitted.
proofSteps: For Q>0 index the family by the native dependent sum of q∈Fin Q and u∈(ZMod(q+1))ˣ, assigning the real point val(u)/(q+1). Native residue bounds and unit coprimality give the hypotheses of reduced-fraction-separation.
Distinct labels give distinct reduced pairs: equal moduli and equal natural representatives imply equal residues and then equal units. Thus the family is separated by δ=Q⁻².
Apply the inherited additive_largeSieve with this positive δ. The additive companion of Finset.prod_sigma rewrites its single family sum as the displayed double sum. Substitute 2/δ=2Q².
For Q=0 the modulus indexing type is empty and the right side is nonnegative. H=0 is already admitted by the inherited theorem.
acceptance: Modulus one contributes its single unit at phase zero; it is not discarded.
The source Theorem 16.1 has H−1+Q². This node deliberately uses the weaker H+2Q² supported by the inherited additive theorem.

sources.match: Same reduced-residue specialization, with an explicitly different inherited additive constant; no claim to have decomposed the sharp additive input.

nodes.title: Integer phase of the standard residue character
nodes.statement: For u∈ZMod q and n∈ℤ, stdAddChar(u·n)=e(n·val(u)/q).
hypotheses: Use e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit), the existing UnitAddCircle norm, and the native DirichletCharacter ℂ q, its conductor-based IsPrimitive predicate and its inverse. There is no new Fourier, character or Farey carrier.
q is a positive natural number. The finite ring ZMod q and its unit group use their native instances, including the trivial ring q=1. Write φ(q)=q.totient and τ(χ)=gaussSum χ ZMod.stdAddChar.
proofSteps: Replace u by the integer cast of its native natural representative. Combine the residue casts into the cast of the integer product val(u)n.

Apply the native standard-character formula at that integer product and the real Fourier-character formula. Rearrange scalar products in the complex exponential. This also handles negative n and nonunit u.
acceptance: At q=4,u=1,n=−1 the value is −i, detecting a sign reversal.
At q=1 every phase is one, including the unique residue zero.

sources.locator: §16.2, the exponential convention in τ and S
sources.match: Explicit normalization adapter between two existing character APIs; verified by a complete temporary Lean proof.

nodes.title: Squared norm of a primitive Dirichlet Gauss sum
nodes.statement: For a primitive Dirichlet character χ modulo q>0, |τ(χ)|²=q.
hypotheses: Use e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit), the existing UnitAddCircle norm, and the native DirichletCharacter ℂ q, its conductor-based IsPrimitive predicate and its inverse. There is no new Fourier, character or Farey carrier.
q is a positive natural number. The finite ring ZMod q and its unit group use their native instances, including the trivial ring q=1. Write φ(q)=q.totient and τ(χ)=gaussSum χ ZMod.stdAddChar.
χ.IsPrimitive is required; χ≠1 alone is not a substitute at composite modulus.
proofSteps: Conductor invariance under inverse makes χ⁻¹ primitive. The native finite Fourier formula gives Dχ(k)=χ⁻¹(−k)τ(χ), using the unnormalized negative-phase DFT.
Apply the native DFT twice and evaluate at −1. Its inversion formula gives qχ(1)=q. Factoring constants and commuting reflection with DFT identifies the same value as χ(−1)τ(χ⁻¹)τ(χ).

The native Gauss conjugation formula gives conjugate(τ(χ))=gaussSum χ⁻¹ (stdAddChar⁻¹). The inverse additive character is its shift by −1. The native primitive shift theorem identifies this as χ(−1)τ(χ⁻¹).

Combine the two equalities and take real parts of τ(χ)conjugate(τ(χ))=q. This proves the square-norm formula without a finite-field assumption, a squarefree modulus assumption or a new Parseval theorem.
acceptance: For q=1 the unique character is primitive and its Gauss sum is 1. Treating zero as a nonunit in this trivial ring would break the statement.
The principal character modulo 4 has Gauss sum 0 and does not satisfy the conclusion.

sources.match: The source cites the norm formula; the packet supplies its complete route through pinned DFT inversion and primitive character formulas. The algebraic product and real norm were verified by temporary Lean proofs.

nodes.title: Gauss expansion of a finite character sum
nodes.statement: For primitive χ modulo q>0, τ(χ⁻¹)Σ_{j<H}a_jχ(n_j)=Σ_{u∈(Z/qZ)×}χ⁻¹(u)S(val(u)/q).
hypotheses: Use e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit), the existing UnitAddCircle norm, and the native DirichletCharacter ℂ q, its conductor-based IsPrimitive predicate and its inverse. There is no new Fourier, character or Farey carrier.
q is a positive natural number. The finite ring ZMod q and its unit group use their native instances, including the trivial ring q=1. Write φ(q)=q.totient and τ(χ)=gaussSum χ ZMod.stdAddChar.
M is any integer, H and Q are natural numbers, and a:Fin H→ℂ is arbitrary. Write n_j=M+j+1 and S(t)=Σ_{j<H}a_j e(n_j t). Empty intervals and Q=0 are permitted.
χ.IsPrimitive; Q is unused in this single-modulus statement.
proofSteps: Apply the native primitive Gauss-shift theorem to χ⁻¹ and the residue n_j. Inversion of χ⁻¹ yields χ(n_j), even when n_j is not a unit.
Multiply the equality by a_j and sum over the finite interval. Expand the existing Gauss sum and interchange the two finite sums.
Terms indexed by nonunits vanish because χ⁻¹ vanishes there. Reindex the remaining residues by the native unit group; this is a bijection onto the unit residues.
Apply standard-character-phase at each unit and each integer n_j. Collect the inner finite sum S. Multiplication by τ avoids making an unproved nonzero-denominator cancellation.
acceptance: The coefficients can be complex, and M can be negative.
The formula must hold at nonunit frequencies. A formula proved only for gcd(n_j,q)=1 would be insufficient for an arbitrary interval.

sources.locator: §16.2, proof of Theorem 16.2, primitive Gauss expansion
sources.match: Finite weighted consequence of the already implemented shift formula; inverse characters express conjugation without a competing convention.

nodes.title: Parseval identity over Dirichlet characters
nodes.statement: For arbitrary F:(ZMod q)ˣ→ℂ, Σ_{χ mod q}|Σ_u χ⁻¹(u)F(u)|²=φ(q)Σ_u|F(u)|², summing over all Dirichlet characters modulo q.
hypotheses: Use e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit), the existing UnitAddCircle norm, and the native DirichletCharacter ℂ q, its conductor-based IsPrimitive predicate and its inverse. There is no new Fourier, character or Farey carrier.
q is a positive natural number. The finite ring ZMod q and its unit group use their native instances, including the trivial ring q=1. Write φ(q)=q.totient and τ(χ)=gaussSum χ ZMod.stdAddChar.
proofSteps: Expand each squared norm as its complex product with its conjugate. Finite interchange gives a sum over pairs u,v of F(u)conjugate(F(v)) multiplied by Σχχ⁻¹(u)χ(v).

On units the inverse-character value is χ(u⁻¹). Apply the pinned character orthogonality formula with first argument u. Complex numbers have the required roots of unity; q>0 supplies the finite residue and character instances.
Only the diagonal u=v survives, with coefficient φ(q). Units.val is injective, so equality of residues is equality of unit indices. Take real parts to obtain the exact real square-norm identity.
acceptance: For q=4 and F≡1 on the two units, the left side is 4, equal to 2·2. Using q instead of φ(q) gives the wrong normalization.
At q=1 the equality is |F(1)|²=|F(1)|²; no nontriviality of ZMod q is assumed.

sources.match: Finite energy restatement of the existing orthogonality theorem on the unit group, not a new character theory or general Fourier transform.

nodes.title: Primitive character energy at one modulus
nodes.statement: (q/φ(q))Σ_{χ primitive mod q}|Σ_{j<H}a_jχ(n_j)|² ≤ Σ_{u∈(Z/qZ)×}|S(val(u)/q)|².
hypotheses: Use e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit), the existing UnitAddCircle norm, and the native DirichletCharacter ℂ q, its conductor-based IsPrimitive predicate and its inverse. There is no new Fourier, character or Farey carrier.
q is a positive natural number. The finite ring ZMod q and its unit group use their native instances, including the trivial ring q=1. Write φ(q)=q.totient and τ(χ)=gaussSum χ ZMod.stdAddChar.
M is any integer, H and Q are natural numbers, and a:Fin H→ℂ is arbitrary. Write n_j=M+j+1 and S(t)=Σ_{j<H}a_j e(n_j t). Empty intervals and Q=0 are permitted.
proofSteps: For each primitive χ, take squared norms of finite-gauss-expansion. The inverse is primitive, so its Gauss square norm is q. Divide by positive φ(q), obtaining the source weighted identity.
Sum these identities over the finite subset of primitive characters. On the Fourier side only, enlarge that subset to all characters, since every squared modulus is nonnegative.
Apply character-parseval to F(u)=S(val(u)/q). Cancel φ(q)>0. The arithmetic character sum itself is never extended to imprimitive χ using the primitive Gauss formula.
acceptance: The factor is q/φ(q); neither it nor the primitive filter is suppressed.
At modulus one both sides equal |Σ_j a_j|². H=0 gives zero.

sources.locator: §16.2, weighted equality and enlargement to all characters
sources.match: Separates the primitive Gauss identity from the positivity step, preventing an invalid application of that identity to imprimitive characters.

nodes.title: Primitive-character large sieve
nodes.statement: Σ_{1≤q≤Q}(q/φ(q))Σ_{χ primitive mod q}|Σ_{j<H}a_jχ(M+j+1)|² ≤ (H+2Q²)Σ_{j<H}|a_j|².
hypotheses: Use e(t)=(Real.fourierChar t:ℂ)=exp(2πit), the existing UnitAddCircle norm, and the native DirichletCharacter ℂ q, its conductor-based IsPrimitive predicate and its inverse. There is no new Fourier, character or Farey carrier.
M is any integer, H and Q are natural numbers, and a:Fin H→ℂ is arbitrary. Write n_j=M+j+1 and S(t)=Σ_{j<H}a_j e(n_j t). Empty intervals and Q=0 are permitted.
proofSteps: Sum primitive-modulus-energy over moduli 1 through Q, represented in the seed by q∈Fin Q with actual modulus q+1.
Apply reduced-fraction-large-sieve to the resulting double sum of Fourier values. Its constant is exactly H+2Q².
When Q=0 or H=0 the appropriate sums are empty. No asymptotic range, primality of the moduli, coprimality of the frequencies, or restriction on the complex coefficients is introduced.
acceptance: This is the Bombieri–Davenport reduction with the inherited Bombieri constant. It does not claim the source sharp H−1+Q² constant.
The theorem estimates primitive characters of every positive modulus, including nonsquarefree moduli and modulus one. It is not a quadratic-symbol or polynomial-function-field large sieve.

sources.match: Closes the multiplicative reduction from the already decomposed additive estimate; the source sharper additive input remains a separate gap.

nodes.title: Incomplete logarithm
nodes.statement: Construct λ_V:ArithmeticFunction ℝ by λ_V(n)=Σ_{d|n,V<d}Λ(d). This is a cutoff divisor sum, not log(n/V) and not a multiplicative function.
hypotheses: U,V,N,L,M,n,m,ℓ are natural numbers. Divisors are the native positive divisor finsets; n=0 has no divisors. μ is the native integer Möbius function, Λ the native real von Mangoldt function, and log is the real logarithm with its native value at zero.
Write λ_V for incompleteLog V. All cutoffs are inclusive below and strict above. Ioc(a,b) means a<k≤b and is empty when b≤a. No positivity of U or V is needed for the finite identities.
proofSteps: Use the existing zero-preserving arithmetic-function carrier. The finite formula is zero at n=0 because the native divisor finset is empty.

For the convolution proof, let h_V(n) be Λ(n) when V<n and zero otherwise, as a local zero-preserving function. Native convolution with ζ gives λ_V=h_V*ζ by coe_mul_zeta_apply. This local abbreviation is not a new exported truncation carrier.
The source uses V=floor(x^(1/5)); natural V keeps every endpoint exact and admits independent U,V. Its subtraction formula is established by the next lemma.
acceptance: Keep every prime-power divisor, not just prime divisors.
At V=0 the result is the full logarithm, while λ_V(n)=0 for n≤V.

sources.match: Finite native-carrier decomposition of the cited identity. The cutoff and weighted-sum extensions and their proofs are supplied here; none asserts an analytic cancellation estimate.

hypotheses: U,V,N,L,M,n,m,ℓ are natural numbers. Divisors are the native positive divisor finsets; n=0 has no divisors. μ is the native integer Möbius function, Λ the native real von Mangoldt function, and log is the real logarithm with its native value at zero.

proofSteps: Partition the finite positive divisors into V<d and d≤V; these are complementary predicates, including equality.
Apply the native vonMangoldt_sum to the unfiltered sum and rearrange the two real finite sums. At n=0 all divisor sums and the native real logarithm vanish.

No analytic convergence or inversion theorem is needed.

nodes.title: Vanishing below the incomplete-log cutoff
nodes.statement: If n≤V then λ_V(n)=0.
hypotheses: U,V,N,L,M,n,m,ℓ are natural numbers. Divisors are the native positive divisor finsets; n=0 has no divisors. μ is the native integer Möbius function, Λ the native real von Mangoldt function, and log is the real logarithm with its native value at zero.

nodes.title: Möbius inversion of the incomplete logarithm
nodes.statement: (μ*λ_V)(n) equals Λ(n) if V<n and zero otherwise, where μ is cast to ArithmeticFunction ℝ and * is native Dirichlet convolution.
hypotheses: U,V,N,L,M,n,m,ℓ are natural numbers. Divisors are the native positive divisor finsets; n=0 has no divisors. μ is the native integer Möbius function, Λ the native real von Mangoldt function, and log is the real logarithm with its native value at zero.
Write λ_V for incompleteLog V. All cutoffs are inclusive below and strict above. Ioc(a,b) means a<k≤b and is empty when b≤a. No positivity of U or V is needed for the finite identities.
proofSteps: Use the local high-part h_V from the construction and the identity λ_V=h_V*ζ.
In the native commutative convolution ring, μ*(h_V*ζ)=h_V*(μ*ζ)=h_V by the already implemented Möbius–zeta inverse.
Evaluate at n. In particular, this is an identity for all natural n rather than a formula requiring the later small-number error to be discarded.

For V=0 this specializes to the existing μ*log=Λ; it does not replan that library theorem.

nodes.title: Vaughan's identity with its boundary term
nodes.statement: Λ(n)=1_{n≤V}Λ(n)+Σ_{b|n,b≤U}μ(b)log(n/b)−Σ_{b|n,b≤U}μ(b)Σ_{c|n/b,c≤V}Λ(c)+Σ_{b|n,U<b}μ(b)Σ_{c|n/b,V<c}Λ(c). All μ values are cast to ℝ, and n/b is exact natural division at divisor indices.
hypotheses: U,V,N,L,M,n,m,ℓ are natural numbers. Divisors are the native positive divisor finsets; n=0 has no divisors. μ is the native integer Möbius function, Λ the native real von Mangoldt function, and log is the real logarithm with its native value at zero.
Write λ_V for incompleteLog V. All cutoffs are inclusive below and strict above. Ioc(a,b) means a<k≤b and is empty when b≤a. No positivity of U or V is needed for the finite identities.
proofSteps: Expand (μ*λ_V)(n) using native mul_apply and the generated additive companion of prod_divisorsAntidiagonal. This gives Σ_{b|n}μ(b)λ_V(n/b).
Add the complementary boundary 1_{n≤V}Λ(n). By moebius-incomplete-log, the result is Λ(n), including n=0.
Partition b-divisors at b≤U. In the low part insert incomplete-log-sub and distribute the finite sum over subtraction; in the high part insert the construction's tail-divisor formula.

For n>V the boundary term is zero and the result is exactly the source three-term identity. At positive n, c|(n/b) is equivalent to bc|n when b|n, so the nested divisor form has exactly the printed indexing, with no extra multiplicities.
acceptance: At n=V=2 the three nonboundary terms cancel to zero; the retained boundary is log 2.
U=0 and V=0 are permitted; there is no division by a cutoff and no loss factor.

nodes.title: Weighted Vaughan identity on a finite hyperbola
nodes.statement: For arbitrary w:ℕ→ℂ, Σ_{n∈Ioc(0,N)}Λ(n)w(n)=Σ_{n∈Ioc(0,min(N,V))}Λ(n)w(n)+Σ_{m∈Ioc(0,N)}μ(m)Σ_{ℓ∈Ioc(0,⌊N/m⌋)}λ_V(ℓ)w(mℓ). Real and integer coefficients are cast to ℂ.
hypotheses: U,V,N,L,M,n,m,ℓ are natural numbers. Divisors are the native positive divisor finsets; n=0 has no divisors. μ is the native integer Möbius function, Λ the native real von Mangoldt function, and log is the real logarithm with its native value at zero.
Write λ_V for incompleteLog V. All cutoffs are inclusive below and strict above. Ioc(a,b) means a<k≤b and is empty when b≤a. No positivity of U or V is needed for the finite identities.
proofSteps: Evaluate moebius-incomplete-log and separate the boundary at each n. Cast to ℂ, multiply by w(n) and sum; the boundary condition n≤V identifies Ioc(0,min(N,V)).
For the convolution part expand mul_apply. At 0<n≤N rewrite n.divisorsAntidiagonal as the filtered product Ioc(0,N)×Ioc(0,N), using the native divisor-antidiagonal theorem.

Interchange finite sums. For any positive m,ℓ, summing the equality test mℓ=n over n∈Ioc(0,N) leaves the unique term w(mℓ) precisely when mℓ≤N. Thus arbitrary w stays attached to the product, not to either factor separately.

For m>0 the product restriction is ℓ≤⌊N/m⌋. Apply the same finite domain conversion as the pinned unweighted sum_Ioc_mul_eq_sum_sum, now retaining w(mℓ). This is the specialized weighted adapter; the already built unweighted convolution summation is not replanned.
acceptance: N=0 makes every sum empty.
The weight need not be multiplicative, nonnegative, bounded or periodic. Replacing w(mℓ) with w(m)w(ℓ) is invalid.

nodes.title: Exact support of the bilinear Vaughan term
nodes.statement: If λ_V(ℓ)≠0 and mℓ≤N, then V<ℓ and m≤⌊N/(V+1)⌋.
hypotheses: U,V,N,L,M,n,m,ℓ are natural numbers. Divisors are the native positive divisor finsets; n=0 has no divisors. μ is the native integer Möbius function, Λ the native real von Mangoldt function, and log is the real logarithm with its native value at zero.
Write λ_V for incompleteLog V. All cutoffs are inclusive below and strict above. Ioc(a,b) means a<k≤b and is empty when b≤a. No positivity of U or V is needed for the finite identities.
proofSteps: Contraposition of incomplete-log-support gives V<ℓ, hence V+1≤ℓ.
Multiply by m and use mℓ≤N. Since V+1 is positive, native natural division gives m≤N/(V+1). The denominator never vanishes, even at V=0.
acceptance: No converse is claimed: lying in this region does not imply a nonzero coefficient.
For V=2,N=12, ℓ=3,m=4 reaches the exact cofactor endpoint; replacing the bound by a strict inequality would lose it.

nodes.title: Finite Type I–Type II Vaughan decomposition
nodes.statement: Put B=⌊N/(V+1)⌋. For arbitrary w:ℕ→ℂ, Σ_{0<n≤N}Λ(n)w(n)=Σ_{0<n≤min(N,V)}Λ(n)w(n)+Σ_{0<m≤min(U,B)}μ(m)Σ_{V<ℓ≤⌊N/m⌋}λ_V(ℓ)w(mℓ)+Σ_{U<m≤B}μ(m)Σ_{V<ℓ≤⌊N/m⌋}λ_V(ℓ)w(mℓ).
hypotheses: U,V,N,L,M,n,m,ℓ are natural numbers. Divisors are the native positive divisor finsets; n=0 has no divisors. μ is the native integer Möbius function, Λ the native real von Mangoldt function, and log is the real logarithm with its native value at zero.
Write λ_V for incompleteLog V. All cutoffs are inclusive below and strict above. Ioc(a,b) means a<k≤b and is empty when b≤a. No positivity of U or V is needed for the finite identities.
proofSteps: Start with weighted-vaughan-hyperbola. Remove ℓ≤V by incomplete-log-support; every removed summand is zero.
Remove m>B by vaughan-bilinear-support: for every retained inner index, nonzero λ_V(ℓ) would contradict that m-bound. The zero coefficients can be removed without any condition on w.
Partition Ioc(0,B) into Ioc(0,min(U,B)) and Ioc(U,B). These sets are disjoint and cover even if U>B. Distribute the finite sum.

The first block is the small-Möbius-factor Type I contribution; the second is a bilinear sum with both factors above their cutoffs. Its inner upper limit remains dependent on m. Turning this hyperbola into independent rectangles requires a separate analytic argument, not an equality asserted here.
acceptance: Both degenerate regimes U≥B (empty Type II) and V≥N (boundary only) are included.
A point-mass weight at n=V detects loss of the boundary; a complex nonmultiplicative weight detects incorrect weight factoring.
ES.4 may substitute w(n)=e(αn), and SV.3 may substitute progression indicators; neither specialization supplies the required analytic estimates.

nodes.title: Elementary Vaughan coefficient energies
nodes.statement: For L≤M, Σ_{ℓ∈Ioc(L,M)}λ_V(ℓ)²≤(M−L)(log M)² and Σ_{m∈Ioc(L,M)}(μ(m):ℝ)²≤M−L.
hypotheses: U,V,N,L,M,n,m,ℓ are natural numbers. Divisors are the native positive divisor finsets; n=0 has no divisors. μ is the native integer Möbius function, Λ the native real von Mangoldt function, and log is the real logarithm with its native value at zero.
Write λ_V for incompleteLog V. All cutoffs are inclusive below and strict above. Ioc(a,b) means a<k≤b and is empty when b≤a. No positivity of U or V is needed for the finite identities.
proofSteps: If M=0 then L=0 and both sums are empty. Otherwise each index is positive and at most M.
Use incomplete-log-bounds and monotonicity of log on positive inputs to obtain 0≤λ_V(ℓ)≤log M. Square this nonnegative inequality and sum.
Use the native |μ(m)|≤1, cast from ℤ to ℝ, square and sum. The two constant sums have cardinal M−L by the native interval cardinality formula.
These coefficient-only upper bounds are available to a later bilinear Cauchy–Schwarz step. They claim no cancellation and do not turn the dependent hyperbola into a rectangle.
acceptance: At L=M both energies are zero.

nodes.title: Primitive character energy on a dyadic band
nodes.statement: Σ_{P<q≤2P}φ(q)⁻¹Σχ*|Aχ|² ≤ ((H+8P²)/P)E_a.
hypotheses: M,N are arbitrary integers; H,K are natural interval lengths; a:Fin H→ℂ and b:Fin K→ℂ are arbitrary. Write Aχ=Σ_{j<H}a_jχ(M+j+1), Bχ=Σ_{j<K}b_jχ(N+j+1), E_a=Σ|a_j|² and E_b=Σ|b_j|². Character values use the native residue cast.

φ(q) is the native totient. Every character sum is over primitive Dirichlet characters modulo the positive integer q. Write T(R,Q)=Σ_{R<q≤Q}φ(q)⁻¹Σχ*|Aχ||Bχ|; this is display notation, not a new carrier or bound predicate. Empty intervals and zero coefficients are allowed.
P is a positive natural number.
proofSteps: For each q>P, φ(q)>0 and 1/φ(q)≤q/(Pφ(q)). Multiply by the nonnegative primitive character energy.
Extend the resulting positive sum to all 1≤q≤2P, factor out 1/P, and apply primitive-large-sieve with upper cutoff 2P.
The inherited constant is H+2(2P)²=H+8P². The source sharper H−1+4P² is not substituted for it.

For P=2 the band is {3,4}: q=2 is excluded and q=4 retained.
No application of a primitive Gauss identity to imprimitive characters occurs.

nodes.statement: T(P,2P) ≤ P⁻¹√(H+8P²)√(K+8P²)√E_a√E_b.
hypotheses: M,N are arbitrary integers; H,K are natural interval lengths; a:Fin H→ℂ and b:Fin K→ℂ are arbitrary. Write Aχ=Σ_{j<H}a_jχ(M+j+1), Bχ=Σ_{j<K}b_jχ(N+j+1), E_a=Σ|a_j|² and E_b=Σ|b_j|². Character values use the native residue cast.

proofSteps: Flatten the finite family of pairs (q,χ), P<q≤2P and χ primitive. Apply real finite Cauchy–Schwarz to the entries |Aχ|/√φ(q) and |Bχ|/√φ(q).

The single common character in the two factors is retained, not replaced by two independently summed characters.

nodes.title: Finite sum of the bilinear dyadic coefficients
nodes.statement: For real R>0, H,K≥0 and natural J, put P_i=R2^i. Then Σ_{i<J}√(H+8P_i²)√(K+8P_i²)/P_i ≤ 9R(2^J−1)+3J(√H+√K)+(2/R)(1−2^(−J))√H√K.
hypotheses: R is a positive real number; H and K are nonnegative real numbers; J is natural, including zero. The reciprocal power is 2^(−J)=(1/2)^J, never natural subtraction in an exponent.
proofSteps: For any P>0 and X≥0, square the nonnegative proposed upper bound √X+3P to prove √(X+8P²)≤√X+3P. This is deliberately weaker than using √8.
Multiply the two bounds and divide by P. The result is at most 9P+3(√H+√K)+√H√K/P.
Sum the first and last terms using the existing finite geometric-sum formula with ratios 2 and 1/2: ΣP_i=R(2^J−1) and Σ1/P_i=(2/R)(1−(1/2)^J).
The middle term does not decay with i and contributes exactly 3J(√H+√K). Retain this factor; dropping it is not justified by the block estimates. All expressions vanish at J=0.
acceptance: At H=K=0, R=2,J=3 the left side is 112; the displayed upper bound is 126.
At J=0 both sides are zero.
The scale-independent sum over four bands is four times its summand, not once.

nodes.statement: If R>0 and Q≤R2^J≤2Q, then T(R,Q) ≤ [18Q+3J(√H+√K)+(2/R)√H√K]√E_a√E_b.
hypotheses: M,N are arbitrary integers; H,K are natural interval lengths; a:Fin H→ℂ and b:Fin K→ℂ are arbitrary. Write Aχ=Σ_{j<H}a_jχ(M+j+1), Bχ=Σ_{j<K}b_jχ(N+j+1), E_a=Σ|a_j|² and E_b=Σ|b_j|². Character values use the native residue cast.

φ(q) is the native totient. Every character sum is over primitive Dirichlet characters modulo the positive integer q. Write T(R,Q)=Σ_{R<q≤Q}φ(q)⁻¹Σχ*|Aχ||Bχ|; this is display notation, not a new carrier or bound predicate. Empty intervals and zero coefficients are allowed.

nodes.title: Level of distribution of the primes (Maynard (1.3))
nodes.statement: For real θ the primes have level of distribution θ if, for every A>0, Σ_{1≤q≤x^θ} max_{(a,q)=1} |π(x;q,a) − π(x)/φ(q)| = O_A(x/(log x)^A) as x→∞. Here π(x;q,a) counts the primes p≤x with p≡a (mod q), π(x) counts all primes p≤x and φ is Euler's function. The Elliott–Halberstam conjecture is the statement that the primes have level of distribution θ for every θ<1.
hypotheses: x is real; q runs over the integers 1≤q≤⌊x^θ⌋ and a over the reduced residues 0≤a<q. The term q=1 vanishes identically.
The comparison term is π(x)/φ(q), counting all primes up to x, exactly as in Maynard (1.3). His footnote 1 notes that other authors use slightly different definitions; this node fixes (1.3).
Elliott–Halberstam is a named hypothesis. No node of this roadmap asserts it, and every consumer carries it as an explicit hypothesis (RS-07).
proofSteps: Define π(x;q,a) as the number of primes p≤⌊x⌋ with p≡a (mod q), the discrepancy as the supremum over reduced residues a<q of |π(x;q,a) − π(x)/φ(q)|, and PrimesHaveLevel θ as the family of big-O statements along x→∞ indexed by A>0.

Define windowError(N,q) = 1 + sup_{(a,q)=1} |#{N≤n<2N : n prime, n≡a} − #{N≤n<2N : n prime}/φ(q)|, which is Maynard's E(N,q) of (5.16). The window API follows from the level estimates at x=2N−1 and x=N−1, since windowError(N,q) ≤ 1 + discrepancy(2N−1,q) + discrepancy(N−1,q), together with Σ_{q≤N^θ′}1 ≤ N^θ′ for θ′<θ<1.
Monotonicity in θ: for x≥1 the sum over q≤x^θ′ is a subsum of the sum over q≤x^θ, and every term is nonnegative. For θ≤0 only q=1 can occur.
acceptance: The level is a statement for every A>0, with an implied constant depending on A. It is not a single-A bound.
Levels θ>1 fail (non-example test), so the Elliott–Halberstam range θ<1 is the natural limit. The Friedlander–Granville obstruction that Maynard mentions (p. 384) is not planned here.

nodes.title: Bombieri–Vinogradov: every level θ<1/2
nodes.statement: For every θ<1/2 the primes have level of distribution θ in the sense of Maynard (1.3).
hypotheses: The input is the ψ-form Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem, Kedlaya Theorem 18.4: for every A>0 there are c(A) and B(A) with Σ_{N≤Q} max_{m∈(ℤ/Nℤ)^×} |ψ(x;N,m) − x/φ(N)| ≤ c·x(log x)^{−A} for Q = x^{1/2}(log x)^{−B}. Its proof is the SV.3 decomposition still to be done (gap 'SV.3 remaining source decomposition').
The conclusion compares with π(x)/φ(q), as Maynard does, and not with li(x)/φ(q).
proofSteps: Input: Kedlaya Theorem 18.4. Its N=1 term alone gives |ψ(x) − x| ≤ c·x(log x)^{−A}.

Prime powers: in every progression |ψ(t;q,a) − θ(t;q,a)| ≤ |ψ(t) − θ(t)| ≤ 2√t·log t (Mathlib abs_psi_sub_theta_le_sqrt_mul_log). Summed over q≤x^θ this costs O(x^{θ+1/2} log x), which is O(x/(log x)^A) because θ<1/2.

Abel summation with f = 1/log (sum_mul_eq_sub_sub_integral_mul): π(x;q,a) = θ(x;q,a)/log x + ∫_2^x θ(t;q,a)/(t log²t) dt, and the same holds for π(x) with θ(t). Hence |π(x;q,a) − π(x)/φ(q)| ≤ E(x;q)/log x + ∫_2^x E(t;q)/(t log²t) dt + φ(q)^{−1}(|θ(x) − x|/log x + ∫_2^x |θ(t) − t|/(t log²t) dt), where E(t;q) = max_{(a,q)=1} |θ(t;q,a) − t/φ(q)|.

Split the integrals at t₀ = x/(log x)^{A+2}. For t≤t₀ the trivial bound E(t;q) ≤ (t/q + 1 + t/φ(q))·log t suffices. For t₀<t≤x and x large, x^θ ≤ t^{1/2}(log t)^{−B} because θ<1/2, so Theorem 18.4 at t covers every q≤x^θ.
Sum over q≤x^θ using Σ_{q≤y} 1/φ(q) = O(log y). Every term is O(x/(log x)^A).
acceptance: θ<1/2 is strict: the theorem gives no level 1/2 (Maynard, p. 384).
Instance: θ = 1/2 − ε is the input of Maynard Theorem 1.3.
The implied constants are ineffective, through Siegel's theorem inside Theorem 18.4. Maynard's remark after Lemma 5.2 records this.

nodes.title: Selberg's diagonal sum in dimension one (GGPY Lemma 3, κ=1)
nodes.statement: Under (Ω₁) and (Ω₂(1,L)), the partial products of ∏_p (1 − γ(p)/p)^{−1}(1 − 1/p) converge to some c_γ, and for z≥2, Σ_{d<z} μ²(d)g(d) = c_γ log z + O(c_γ L). The implied constant depends only on A₁ and A₂.
hypotheses: γ is multiplicative, A₁>1, A₂≥0 and L≥1. (Ω₁): 0 ≤ γ(p)/p ≤ 1 − 1/A₁ for every prime p. (Ω₂(1,L)): −L ≤ Σ_{w≤p<z} γ(p)log p/p − log(z/w) ≤ A₂ for 2≤w≤z. g(d) = ∏_{p|d} γ(p)/(p − γ(p)) on squarefree d. GGPY state (2.3) as γ(p)/p ≤ 1 − 1/A₁; Maynard's Lemma 6.1 writes 1 − A₁, an equivalent reparametrization.
Only squarefree d contribute, so g need only be defined on squarefree integers. Maynard calls it totally multiplicative.
proofSteps: Outline only: the source proof is Halberstam–Richert, Lemmas 5.3–5.4, which was not read (gap). Write G(y) = Σ_{d<y} μ²(d)g(d). For squarefree d, log d = Σ_{p|d} log p, so Σ_{d<z} μ²(d)g(d) log d = Σ_{p<z} g(p) log p·G_p(z/p), where G_p is G restricted to d coprime to p.
By (Ω₁), G_p(y) = G(y) + O(g(p)G(y)) and Σ_p g(p)² log p = O_{A₁}(1). By (Ω₂) and Abel summation, Σ_{p<z} g(p) log p·G(z/p) = ∫_1^z G(u) du/u + O((L+1)G(z)).

Abel summation on the left-hand side gives G(z) log z − ∫_1^z G(t) dt/t. Hence G(z) log z = 2∫_1^z G(t) dt/t + O((L+1)G(z)). The solution of this integral relation is G(z) = c·log z + O(cL), by the Levin–Fainleib iteration in H–R Lemma 5.3.

Identify c = c_γ. The Dirichlet series Σ μ²(d)g(d)d^{−s} equals ζ(s+1)H(s) with H(s) = ∏_p (1 + g(p)p^{−s})(1 − p^{−1−s}), and H(0) = c_γ. Convergence of the partial products follows from (Ω₂) and Mertens' estimate Σ_{w≤p<z} log p/p = log(z/w) + O(1) (requested from AN.2), by partial summation against 1/log p.
acceptance: γ(p) = 1 for p∤W and γ(p) = 0 for p|W gives g(d) = 1/φ(d) on d coprime to W and c_γ = φ(W)/W, so Σ_{d<z,(d,W)=1} μ²(d)/φ(d) = (φ(W)/W)(log z + O(L)) with L ≪ 1 + Σ_{p|W} log p/p (Maynard (6.7)–(6.8)).
The constant is independent of L and of γ beyond A₁ and A₂. Maynard uses this uniformity with L ≪ log log N.

nodes.title: Smoothly weighted diagonal sum (Maynard Lemma 6.1, GGPY Lemma 4)
nodes.statement: Under (Ω₁) and (Ω₂(1,L)), for G: [0,1]→ℝ of class C¹ with G_max = sup_{[0,1]}(|G| + |G′|): Σ_{d<z} μ²(d)g(d)G(log d/log z) = c_γ log z ∫_0^1 G(x) dx + O(c_γ L G_max). The implied constant depends only on A₁ and A₂, not on L or G.
hypotheses: γ is multiplicative, A₁>1, A₂≥0 and L≥1. (Ω₁): 0 ≤ γ(p)/p ≤ 1 − 1/A₁ for every prime p. (Ω₂(1,L)): −L ≤ Σ_{w≤p<z} γ(p)log p/p − log(z/w) ≤ A₂ for 2≤w≤z. g(d) = ∏_{p|d} γ(p)/(p − γ(p)) on squarefree d. GGPY state (2.3) as γ(p)/p ≤ 1 − 1/A₁; Maynard's Lemma 6.1 writes 1 − A₁, an equivalent reparametrization.
GGPY state Lemma 4 for piecewise differentiable F evaluated at log(z/d)/log z. With G(x) = F(1−x) this is Maynard's form, with ∫_0^1 G = ∫_0^1 F(1−x) dx. Maynard writes S for c_γ.
proofSteps: Write the sum as the Stieltjes integral ∫_{1−}^{z} G(log u/log z) d𝒢(u), where 𝒢(u) = Σ_{d<u} μ²(d)g(d) = c_γ log u + E(u) and |E(u)| ≤ C c_γ L by SV.1/selberg-diagonal-sum-dimension-one.
Main part: the substitution u = z^x gives c_γ log z ∫_0^1 G(x) dx.
The E part: integrate by parts (Abel summation). The boundary terms are at most G_max·C c_γ L, and ∫_1^z |E(u)||G′(log u/log z)| du/(u log z) ≤ C c_γ L G_max.
acceptance: Maynard applies it with γ from (6.7), (6.11) and (6.19), obtaining (6.9), (6.13) and (6.21).
G ≡ 1 recovers SV.1/selberg-diagonal-sum-dimension-one.

nodes.title: Admissible tuple
nodes.statement: A finite set H of nonnegative integers is admissible if, for every prime p, there is an integer a_p with a_p ≢ h (mod p) for every h∈H.
hypotheses: H is a Finset ℕ. The empty set is admissible. Only primes p≤#H can obstruct admissibility, since #H elements meet at most #H residue classes.
proofSteps: Define IsAdmissible H as: for every prime p there is a with ¬ h ≡ a [MOD p] for all h∈H.
Characterisation: H misses a class mod p exactly when the image of reduction mod p has fewer than p elements, which is automatic for p>#H. This makes the predicate decidable.
Monotonicity under subsets and invariance under translation h ↦ h+c (replace a_p by a_p + c) are immediate.
isAdmissible_of_forall_not_dvd: if no element is divisible by a prime p≤#H, residue 0 is missed for those p.

nodes.title: The prime k-tuples conjecture, as a named statement
nodes.statement: For a finite H⊂ℕ let primeTranslates(H) = {n : n+h is prime for every h∈H}. The prime k-tuples conjecture asserts that primeTranslates(H) is infinite for every admissible H.
hypotheses: It is a named statement, not an assumption. RS-07 moves the prime-tuple statement register here from AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.6, separately from Maynard's proven theorems.
proofSteps: Define primeTranslates and PrimeTuplesConjecture as displayed.
Necessity: if H covers every class mod p, then for each n some n+h is divisible by p, hence equals p. So n ≤ p, and primeTranslates(H) is finite.
The singleton {0} gives the set of primes (Mathlib infinite_setOfPred_prime), and {0,2} gives the twin primes.
acceptance: Maynard's proven statement (SV.4/positive-proportion-prime-tuples) is a positive-proportion result, not this conjecture. The twin prime conjecture is the case H = {0,2}, and it is not proved.

nodes.title: The W-trick residue v₀ (Maynard (4.1))
nodes.statement: For real D₀ let W = ∏_{p≤D₀} p, the primorial of ⌊D₀⌋. For admissible H there is v₀ with 0≤v₀<W and gcd(v₀+h, W) = 1 for every h∈H; wResidue(H,D₀) is the least such v₀ (0 if none exists). Maynard takes D₀ = log log log N, and then W ≪ (log log N)².
hypotheses: H is admissible. Only ⌊D₀⌋ matters.
AdditiveCombinatorics:AC.4 plans a separate W-trick for the Green–Tao majorant (one linear form). RS-07 keeps the two apart; this is the tuple version.
proofSteps: For each prime p≤D₀, admissibility gives a class a_p missed by H. Require v₀ ≡ −a_p (mod p); then v₀+h ≡ h − a_p ≢ 0 (mod p) for every h∈H.
The primes p≤D₀ are pairwise coprime, so Nat.chineseRemainderOfFinset gives v₀ mod W. Minimality: take Nat.find of the decidable existence statement over v<W.
W ≤ 4^{⌊D₀⌋} ≤ 4^{D₀} by primorial_le_four_pow. With D₀ = log log log N, 4^{D₀} = (log log N)^{log 4} ≤ (log log N)² for large N.
acceptance: For H = {0,2} and D₀ = 3: W = 6 and v₀ = 5, since 5 and 7 are both coprime to 6.

nodes.title: Maynard's multidimensional sieve weights
nodes.statement: Fix k, W, R>1 and F: ℝ^k→ℝ. For r∈ℕ^k put y_r = F(log r₁/log R, …, log r_k/log R) when ∏rᵢ is squarefree, coprime to W and less than R, and y_r = 0 otherwise (6.3). Define λ_d = (∏ μ(dᵢ)dᵢ) Σ_{r: dᵢ|rᵢ} y_r/∏φ(rᵢ) (5.8), and the weight w_n = (Σ_{dᵢ|n+hᵢ ∀i} λ_d)² (2.4). With these, S₁ = Σ_{N≤n<2N, n≡v₀ (W)} w_n, S₂^{(m)} = Σ_{same n} χ_P(n+h_m)w_n, and y^{(m)}_r = (∏ μ(rᵢ)g(rᵢ)) Σ_{rᵢ|dᵢ, d_m=1} λ_d/∏φ(dᵢ), where g is totally multiplicative with g(p) = p−2 ((4.2), (5.14), (5.23)).
hypotheses: λ built from a general y (maynardLambdaOfY) is what Lemmas 5.1–5.3 use; maynardLambda specializes to (6.3). Proposition 4.1 writes λ directly from F and replaces ∏rᵢ<R by 'F supported on ℛ_k'. The two differ only at ∏rᵢ = R, which does not affect the asymptotics.
All sums are finite: rᵢ and dᵢ run below ⌈R⌉, and every other term vanishes by the support condition.
proofSteps: Define y, λ, w, S₁, S₂^{(m)}, g and y^{(m)} as displayed.
Support: if dᵢ|rᵢ for all i, then ∏dᵢ divides ∏rᵢ. So some y_r in the sum can be nonzero only if ∏dᵢ is squarefree, coprime to W and less than R.
Inversion (5.7)–(5.8): substitute the definition and use Σ_{dᵢ|rᵢ|eᵢ} μ(rᵢ) = μ(dᵢ)·[eᵢ = dᵢ] for squarefree eᵢ.
Dimension one: (Σ_{d|m} λ_d)² = Σ_{e|m} Σ_{lcm(d₁,d₂)=e} λ_{d₁}λ_{d₂} = Σ_{e|m} lambdaSquared(λ)(e).
acceptance: For R = 2 only r = (1,…,1) is supported, so λ_{(1,…,1)} = F(0), every other λ_d vanishes, and w_n = F(0)² for every n.
The weights depend on (d₁,…,d_k) jointly, not only on ∏dᵢ. This is the new feature of the method (p. 387).

nodes.title: Maynard's variational quantity M_k
nodes.statement: Let ℛ_k = {t∈[0,1]^k : Σtᵢ ≤ 1}. For F: [0,1]^k→ℝ put I_k(F) = ∫F² and J_k^{(m)}(F) = ∫(∫_0^1 F dt_m)² dt₁…dt_{m−1}dt_{m+1}…dt_k. Let 𝒮_k be the set of F supported on ℛ_k with I_k(F) ≠ 0 and J_k^{(m)}(F) ≠ 0 for every m. Then M_k = sup_{F∈𝒮_k} Σ_m J_k^{(m)}(F)/I_k(F).
hypotheses: Maynard's 𝒮_k consists of Riemann-integrable functions; here it consists of square-integrable functions on the cube. The suprema agree: every Riemann-integrable function is square-integrable, and SV.4/ratio-smooth-approximation approximates every square-integrable member by smooth functions supported on ℛ_k.
J^{(m)} is integrated over the whole cube. Its integrand does not depend on t_m, so this is the (k−1)-fold integral of the source.
G_{b,j} of Lemma 8.1 is included as data, with the r = 0 term (E31).
proofSteps: Define ℛ_k, I_k, J_k^{(m)}, the admissible class, the ratio, and M_k as the supremum of a set of reals bounded above by k.
Upper bound: by Cauchy–Schwarz, (∫_0^1 F dt_m)² ≤ ∫_0^1 F² dt_m. So J^{(m)} ≤ I and M_k ≤ k.
Replacing F by cF multiplies I and each J^{(m)} by c². Permuting the coordinates permutes the J^{(m)}.
Radial case F = G(Σtᵢ) on ℛ_k: slice by s = Σ_{i≠m} tᵢ, whose density on ℛ_{k−1} is s^{k−2}/(k−2)!. This gives the GPY integrals of the remark after Lemma 6.3.
acceptance: M₁ = 1: J^{(1)} = (∫F)² ≤ ∫F², with equality for F = 1 on [0,1].
The support condition is essential: F ≡ 1 on the cube has ratio k.
